Consider the table in front of me. What I directly perceive is a set of sense-data: a brown color, a certain shape, a pressure against my hand. The question is whether these data are evidence for an enduring object that exists independently of my perceiving it. The commonsense answer is yes; the skeptical answer notes that I could have exactly these experiences in a dream. One reply is to treat the existence of the object as the simplest hypothesis that explains the regularity of my experiences — that the table appears again when I re-enter the room, and that other people report seeing it too. This argument does not amount to proof; it appeals to simplicity, which is itself an assumption. Still, the alternative requires a far more elaborate account of why experience is so orderly.
